theme: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
queries_run: gh search repos "world cup 2026 schedule dataset"
WebFetch raw READMEs for mominullptr/FIFA-World-Cup-2026-Dataset and italobel/world-cup-2026-calendar

candidates.name: FIFA-World-Cup-2026-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 12 committed CSVs: venues.csv (16 stadiums, city/country/capacity/lat-lon across US/Canada/Mexico), matches.csv + matches_detailed.csv (104 matches, date, kickoff_time_utc, stage, venue_id, teams, scores, xG), teams.csv (48 teams, group, FIFA rank/Elo), squads_and_players.csv (1,248 players), plus match_events, match_team_stats, match_lineups, player_stats, match_prediction_features (65 ML features). Actively updated during the tournament (Jun 11-Jul 19 2026). CC0-1.0 license, 63 stars, updated 30 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #11 (World Cup 2026 host-city/schedule data): venue city + exact match date lets us build a host-city demand-shock calendar for 3Q26 nights/ADR (World Cup falls entirely inside 3Q26). Capacity and lat/lon support a per-market intensity weight (e.g. more matches/bigger stadium in a metro = larger STR demand pulse) for NA markets in the Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.size_hint: 12 CSV files, largest ~1,248 rows (players); matches.csv 104 rows

candidates.name: world-cup-2026-calendar
candidates.what_it_holds: Single committed FIFA_World_Cup_2026.ics file (~40KB), all 104 matches numbered WC2026 #1-#104, group letters A-L, kickoff times in US Eastern, venue and host city for every match (Estadio Azteca, MetLife Stadium, BMO Field, AT&T Stadium, etc.) across US/Canada/Mexico, Jun 11-Jul 19 2026. MIT license, 6 stars, updated 23 Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same schedule/host-city gap as above but as a clean, single-file calendar (easy to parse to a date x host-metro table) rather than a relational dataset -- a cheap cross-check/alternate source for the World Cup demand-shock calendar feeding 3Q26 forecasts.

candidates.name: worldcup
candidates.what_it_holds: NestJS/Fastify/Drizzle/PostgreSQL backend shipping a 'pre-loaded dataset (teams, full squads, fixtures, venues, standings, broadcasts, 30+ language names, content) from public sources', plug-and-play via Docker. REST+WebSocket API over the seeded data.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent source for World Cup fixtures/venues with a ready seed/migration file (structured schema) that could be used as a cross-check on match dates/venues if the seed data is inspected; lower priority than the two CSV/ICS sources above since it requires standing up a DB.
candidates.size_hint: seed data + Postgres migrations, size not stated

candidates.name: wc2026-events
candidates.what_it_holds: 'FIFA World Cup 2026 match event data - every match, shot maps, xG model, and visualization notebooks.' Likely per-match event-level data with dates/venues embedded; not independently verified beyond description. 26 stars, updated 7 Sep 2026, no license field returned.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional/alternate schedule and venue source with match-level granularity for the 3Q26 World Cup demand-shock calendar; would need a directory listing to confirm files before use.

candidates.name: wc26-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server / AI-tool wrapper with '18 tools covering matches, teams, venues, city guides, fan zones, visa info, head-to-head records' for the 2026 World Cup; works with Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor/Telegram. Likely backed by committed or fetched reference data on host cities and fan zones, not confirmed via directory listing.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying data files (city guides, venue/fan-zone locations) are committed rather than live-fetched, this could add host-city-level detail (fan zones, visa/logistics) beyond just match schedule -- relevant to gauging incremental visitor friction/ease by host market.

candidates.name: python-holidays (vacanza, formerly dr-prodigy/python-holidays)
candidates.what_it_holds: The canonical Python 'holidays' package: programmatic, offline public/bank/school holiday calendars for 100+ countries and many subdivisions, actively maintained (multiple confirmed forks/mirrors seen updated through 2026, e.g. a Sep 2026 l10n-migrator fork and a Rust port 'holidays-rs' both referencing it). MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #20 (holiday calendars by country): gives a clean, versionable, no-API-key way to generate country-level holiday-date panels to control for local demand seasonality (long weekends, national holidays) across ABNB's NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC regional splits and around the World Cup window.
candidates.size_hint: Python package, not a static file dump
candidates.last_activity: 2026 (actively maintained; several dependent forks updated Sep 2026)

candidates.name: sdk-py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official PredictHQ Python API client (MIT, 27 stars, updated 5 May 2026). Wraps PredictHQ's Events API (concerts, sports, conferences, festivals, severe weather, school holidays) with an 'attendance'/'PHQ rank' impact score per event/location. Requires a PredictHQ API key (free tier exists but is rate-limited); no data committed in-repo.
candidates.why_useful: Standard, well-documented client for pulling a global multi-category event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) with impact/attendance scores by location -- the general-purpose tool for the whole 'events and shocks' gap (#11), not just World Cup. Method only, not a dataset; a human would need to register for a key.
candidates.time_coverage: current + forward-looking via API (no vintage/historical bulk export)

candidates.name: phq-data-science-docs
candidates.what_it_holds: PredictHQ's data-science documentation repo (MIT, 17 stars, updated 27 Aug 2026); likely contains sample notebooks/feature-engineering guides referencing PredictHQ event-impact data (rank/attendance features), pointing back to the PredictHQ platform for the underlying bulk data.
candidates.why_useful: Could contain worked examples of turning event calendars into demand features (analogous to what we'd want for World Cup / conferences / holidays feeding nights forecasts) even without a full data export.

candidates.name: streamlit-accommodation-demo
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit demo app pulling PredictHQ event data specifically for accommodation-demand forecasting (per the repo purpose: 'Streamlit Accommodation Demo App'). No committed dataset (needs API key), but the method -- event calendar -> accommodation demand -- is exactly the ABNB use case.
candidates.why_useful: A worked reference implementation for turning an event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) into an accommodation-demand signal, i.e. a template method for the World Cup/holiday/conference demand-shock work, even though it requires a paid/free-tier PredictHQ key to run.

candidates.name: aws-sagemaker-demand-forecasting-example
candidates.what_it_holds: AWS SageMaker XGBoost example forecasting 'real demand' using PredictHQ events as exogenous features (MIT license). Method/notebook, not a static dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Another event-driven demand-forecasting method template (events -> XGBoost demand forecast) that could be adapted to nights/ADR around World Cup or major conferences, though it depends on a live PredictHQ feed rather than committed data.

candidates.name: events-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: 'A Python PIP package to fetch events using Ticketmaster API.' MIT license, small (2 stars). No committed data; a thin client requiring a Ticketmaster Discovery API key (free-tier available) to pull concert/event listings by city/date.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight, pip-installable Ticketmaster client that could be used to build a concert/event-density-by-city calendar as a demand-shock proxy for specific STR markets, complementing PredictHQ; low priority since it is a thin wrapper with no unique value over calling the Ticketmaster API directly.

notes: gh search repos for 'world cup 2026 schedule dataset' returned zero results (too many quoted terms); broadening to 'fifa world cup 2026' surfaced the real dataset repos. 'holidays python package' also returned zero; 'python holidays' found the ecosystem around vacanza/python-holidays (the actual top-starred canonical repo did not appear directly in results -- likely already past the 30-result window sorted by stars with many low-star clutter repos ahead of it alphabetically/by-recency; recommend a follow-up scout directly fetch https://github.com/vacanza/python-holidays to confirm star count and exact country list, since gh search text-matching on the word 'holidays' surfaces mostly toy/practice repos rather than ranking the real package first). No results found for Setlist.fm, Songkick, or Olympics 2026/2028 host-city datasets within the 6-call gh search budget; WebSearch was unavailable (session-wide budget exhausted) so those leads are unexplored -- worth a follow-up scout with fresh search budget. PredictHQ itself is a paid platform; only its free/OSS-licensed client libraries and demo apps are catalogued here as 'method', consistent with 'never use paid API keys'. All World Cup match/venue data found is from third-party GitHub reconstructions (not FIFA's own repo), so treat exact kickoff times/venue assignments as needing a light plausibility check before use, though CC0/MIT licensing makes them freely usable regardless of provenance.
